habitat: Thickets and rank grass in thornveld, plus riparian and old cultivated lands, like its host, Jameson's Firefinch.
summary: A fairly common resident. The male has a whitish or pale pink bill and legs. The female has a whitish bill and pink legs. Newman does not describe the body colour. It parasitises Jameson's Firefinch and mimics that species' bell-like note. It is much more common in dry bushveld than the Dusky Indigobird. The Kemp name Purple Widowfinch and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Dusky Indigobird has reddish legs and is less common in dry bushveld.
Village Indigobird has a red bill and red legs.

head.pattern: Whitish or pale pink. Legs: Whitish or pale pink.

calls.description: It mimics the bell-like call-note of Jameson's Firefinch. The grade A call is from near Klerksdorp. The filename is XC631063-3 Purplt Indigobird.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a fairly common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The body colour is not described, so none is stored. The grade A call is from the North West. The Kemp name Purple Widowfinch and the code RB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^11=2048 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 1024–4096.
